correctness.rationale: The normalized centrally symmetric circuit has vertices ±e_1,±e_2,±e_3,±(a,b,c), a,b,c>0. A generating antipodal pair drops exactly when one of four strict convex-hull triangle-inequality chambers fails, producing a 3D crosspolytope and hence an indecomposable six-vertex case. In the eight-vertex region a facet has at most one point from each antipodal pair, and a four-vertex facet forces one of the three signed equalities a+b−c=1, a−b+c=1, −a+b+c=1. With zero or one equalities, connected triangular facets touch all facets, so McMullen’s criterion yields indecomposability. Two equalities reduce, up to permutation, to a=1,b=c=t≠1: the formula Q_t + [−m h,m h], m=min(1,t), h=(0,1/2,1/2), gives an exact Minkowski decomposition with crosspolytope Q_t. The four triangular facets in two components and parallel cross-edges force every summand deformation, modulo translations, into a two-dimensional cone. Its two independent indecomposable factors therefore supply precisely the two extremal rays. All three equalities give a three-segment parallelotope. Returning to original positive edge weights, exactly two equal pairs characterize the decomposable locus. Independently enumerated rational supporting facets and solved exact edge-parallel deformation linear systems corroborate the 1-, 2-, and 3-dimensional nontranslation deformation cones. Finite rational tests are corroboration, not the universal proof.
residual_risks: All-real-parameter summand-cone completeness depends on the standard equivalence between edge-parallel vertex deformations and Minkowski summands and the triangle-component rank argument; the general framework is not formalized in Lean.
Finite samples do not prove the universal statement.

value.rationale: This is a sharp, motivated classification for the smallest graph C4 whose unweighted symmetric edge polytope is decomposable. It identifies exactly how anisotropic edge weights destroy the Minkowski factorization, distinguishes quadrilateral-facet changes from genuine decomposability, and classifies the complete summand cone on the two-equality strata. A future deformation or rigidity study of edge-weighted circuits can need the precise equality loci, not just the unweighted special case.
residual_risks: Only the positive weighted C4 family is treated, not all weighted graphs.

limitations: Weight inequalities are strictly positive; no conclusion for zero/negative weights, other graphs, lattice/Ehrhart invariants or independent expert/formal certification.
One highly relevant old Yost full source inaccessible through authorized Oxford VPN (VPN disconnected); originality is provisional, not proved by failed search.
